subject: Reserved commit structure, true-ups, PO & Net terms for Dedicated GPU pool
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <e.ruiz@finledger.com>

Cc: FinLedger Procurement <procurement@finledger.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@finledger.com>
Date: 2026-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify billing structure for Dedicated GPU pool

Hi Connor,

Thanks for the demo last week — the Dedicated offering looks promising. Before we move to contract, procurement needs a clearer picture of how billing works for the reserved GPU pool. A few specific asks: 

- If we commit to X GPUs, can you confirm the monthly invoice cadence for (a) monthly prepay, (b) annual prepay?
- How do true-ups work mid-year if usage spikes above committed throughput?
- What discount bands apply for annual prepay vs monthly reserved commits?
- We will need to issue a PO — do you accept PO + Net 30? Any exceptions for Net 45 / Net 60?

Attached: our procurement checklist (we'll forward a formal PO once terms are agreed).

Appreciate a concise summary we can include in our SOW.

Best,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Procurement, FinLedger

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <e.ruiz@finledger.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Clarify billing structure for Dedicated GPU pool

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary below; I'll attach the updated quote and a short example true-up calc. Marissa and Rishi are looped in for model sizing and commercial terms.

1) Billing cadence
  - Monthly prepay: Invoices issued on the 1st of each month for that month's committed capacity. Payment due Net 30 by default.
  - Annual prepay: One invoice for the full year at effective discounted rate; invoice issued upon signature or at kickoff (per customer preference).

2) Discount bands (summary)
  - Monthly reserved commit: baseline rate (no prepay discount).
  - 6–11 month prepay: 6% discount on list for the committed baseline (applies when customer prepays >= 6 months).
  - 12 month annual prepay: 15% discount off baseline for the committed GPU pool.

3) True-ups
  - Usage above committed throughput is billed at the same day-rate but reconciled monthly. For annual prepay customers we apply a quarterly true-up and allow a single mid-year repricing if sustained demand > 125% of committed throughput for two consecutive months.
  - Example (attached): if committed throughput is 1,000 request-units/day and you sustained 1,300 RU/day for May–June, the extra is invoiced on the next monthly invoice and counts toward next quarter's reconciliation.

4) PO & Net terms
  - We accept POs. Standard is Net 30 (Redwood_Terms_Net30.pdf attached). For enterprise customers on annual prepay we can consider Net 45 for the initial invoice with finance approval.

Attachments: FinLedger_Redwood_Dedicated_Quote_v3.pdf, SOW_GPU_Pool_Sizing.xlsx, Redwood_Terms_Net30.pdf

Next steps: Marissa, can you confirm the throughput SLAs and whether we can offer Net 45 on the annual invoice? Also attaching a 1-page mutual action plan template to speed approvals.

Thanks,
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Clarify billing structure for Dedicated GPU pool

Elena — quick note on sizing & SLOs. Connor's summary is accurate; a few specifics to include in the SOW: 

- GPU pool sizing: we recommend an initial pool of 8xA10G equivalent nodes for the workloads you demoed (approx. 350–450 QPS sustained for standard generation paths). See SOW_GPU_Pool_Sizing.xlsx for the workload-to-pool mapping.
- Throughput guarantee: we commit to 99.5% availability at the committed throughput. If we fail to meet throughput SLOs in a calendar month, we issue service credits pro-rated to the affected capacity bucket.
- Reserved commit pricing is tied to an agreed baseline RU/day; bursting above baseline triggers the true-up described by Connor.

On Net terms: we are prepared to offer Net 45 on the initial annual prepay invoice for customers with approved credit — request can be submitted with the PO and will route to finance. Net 60 is uncommon for prepaid structures.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales — Dedicated Solutions

Subject: RE: Clarify billing structure for Dedicated GPU pool — details and sample PO

Carlos — answered inline below and attaching a sample PO + invoice instructions:

1) Sample PO language: see attached template (FinLedger_Redwood_Dedicated_Quote_v3.pdf includes suggested PO text). Key lines to include: 
  - SKU: Redwood Dedicated GPU Pool (8x A10G equiv)
  - Term: 12 months
  - Annual prepay amount: $XXX,XXX (per attached quote)
  - Billing instructions: Invoices to be sent to AP@finledger.com; Redwood payment remittance instructions included in Redwood_Terms_Net30.pdf

2) True-up reconciliation timing: calendar-month based. Overages are captured in the calendar month they occur and appear as a separate line item on your next monthly invoice. For annual prepay customers we do a quarterly aggregated reconciliation to avoid micro-billing; the net overage is either credited or invoiced depending on prior prepay balance.

3) Early termination: For annual prepay we offer a staged unwind: if you downscale before month 6 there is a 20% unwind fee on the remaining prepay balance; month 6–9 is a 10% unwind; after month 9 we allow a one-time 50% rebate of the unused prepay if we can re-allocate capacity. We can make exceptions for force majeure or material breaches.

Attached: FinLedger_Redwood_Dedicated_Quote_v3.pdf, Redwood_Terms_Net30.pdf

Let me know if you want us to drop this language into your standard PO format and we'll prepare a redline-ready doc.

Best,
